title: powerkit whole-study simulation specification
description: Experimental. One population model for a whole study, from which every planned analysis is simulated on the same data sets (run_whole_study()). Each analysis is fitted with its own model, as it would be analysed on its own. The schema checks structure; validate_whole_study() in R checks that the analyses, variables and paths fit together and that the population is possible.
$comment: spec_version 0.1. Keep old versions readable when the format changes.

variables.description: Keyed by role: X (predictor), Y (outcome), W (moderator, if any analysis has one), and M, or M1 and M2, for the mediators. All are scores (continuous) in this version.

mediators.description: With two mediators (M1, M2): side by side (parallel, PROCESS model 4) or in a chain (serial, PROCESS model 6).

paths.description: Standardised path coefficients of the population model, keyed 'From->To'; product terms join the two variables ('XW->Y', 'XW->M', 'MW->Y'). Every path of the model the analyses imply must be given; use 0 for no effect.

correlations.description: 'X<->W': the correlation of X and W. 'M1<->M2': with parallel mediators, the correlation of their residuals.

analyses.description: The planned analyses, each fitted to every simulated data set with its own model. x_y: the regression of Y on X alone (the test of the correlation). interaction: Y on X, W and X x W, testing X x W. indirect: the mediation model, testing the indirect effect along 'path' by a Monte Carlo confidence interval. index_of_mome: moderated mediation (PROCESS model 7 if W moderates X -> M, model 14 if W moderates M -> Y), testing the index of moderated mediation by a Monte Carlo confidence interval.

claim.description: How the main analyses support the study's claim. each: every main result is a separate claim, each tested at alpha. all: the claim needs every main result to be significant, each tested at alpha (joint power is the chance that all are). any: any one significant main result supports the claim, each main test at alpha divided by the number of main analyses (Bonferroni; joint power is the chance that at least one is).

goal.description: power: the power at a fixed total sample size n (analysed). sample_size: the smallest n whose power reaches 'power' (with one main analysis, its power; with several, the chance that all are significant under the claim 'all', that at least one is under 'any', and the power of each under 'each'). A search simulates every analysis at many n, so it is slow: run it on your own computer (export_whole_study_script()).
